startup.name: Layers
startup.one_liner: Measure, understand and track how you look to improve it
startup.description: A consumer product that treats appearance and health as an engineering problem, measuring the body and face, explaining the results and tracking change over time. Revenue model is most likely a subscription or products sold on top of the measurements.

yc_acceptance.basis: YC publishes no acceptance rate; the working prior is about 1 percent with a band of 0.6 to 2 percent (references/yc_acceptance.md). This company is already in the batch named in the input, so the number is for completeness only. Two person team, consumer health, no traction stated: slightly below the typical applicant on team depth, near it on idea novelty, so about 1.2 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: The description is a thesis, not a product: it names no measurement method, no customer and no revenue. YC partners tend to pass on consumer appearance ideas where the repeat usage is unclear, and the looksmaxxing app category is crowded with free face scoring apps, so the most plausible no is weak differentiation and unproven retention.

technical_complexity.rationale: Face and body measurement with computer vision is available off the shelf and a small team can ship an app in weeks; the hard part is validated accuracy and clinically sound advice, which a two person team cannot easily build.

narrative.headline: A thesis stage consumer appearance app with a normal seed chance inside a 13 month window and little reason to expect more.
narrative.general_summary: Layers has a broad thesis about measuring and improving appearance with a two person team. Within the 13.4 month window the cohort anchor for consumer seed rounds is about 42 percent ever, so the window figure is near 25 percent. Consumer appearance is a crowded category with weak monetisation data, so there is no reason to lift above the anchor. These odds do not separate this company from others in the batch. Appearance improvement is a large consumer interest, but the input names no product, customer or revenue, so investors would be funding a thesis. The scored numbers are window specific and anchored on older cohorts, and the remaining risk is mostly execution and timing rather than the idea alone.

assumptions: Description is a thesis with no product detail, so odds follow cohort anchors.
